hints: Read the vertical boundary as Re(z)=2 and use a shaded test point to choose its side.
Read the circle centre as 1−2i and radius 2, then use a test point to choose the inside.
Include equality on both boundaries and write the two conditions in complex notation.
walkthrough:
Identify the vertical boundary line parallel to the imaginary axis:
$$\text{The line passes through } x = 2 \text{ on the real axis: } \operatorname{Re}(z) = 2$$
$$\text{Since the shaded region lies to the right and boundaries are included: } \operatorname{Re}(z) \geqslant 2$$

Identify the circular boundary from the Argand diagram:
$$\text{Center: } c = 1 - 2\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Radius: } r = 2$$
$$\text{Equation of the circle: } |z - (1 - 2\mathrm{i})| = 2$$

Formulate the inequality representing the disk interior and boundary:
$$|z - (1 - 2\mathrm{i})| \leqslant 2 \quad (\text{or } |z - 1 + 2\mathrm{i}| \leqslant 2)$$

State the two inequalities defining the region:
$$\operatorname{Re}(z) \geqslant 2 \quad \text{and} \quad |z - (1 - 2\mathrm{i})| \leqslant 2$$

hints: The least argument is the most clockwise ray from the origin that still reaches the shaded region.
Intersect the boundary x=2 with the circle (x−1)²+(y+2)²=4 and choose the lower point (2,−2−√3).
Use atan2 with that point to preserve the quadrant, and report the angle to 3 significant figures in degrees or radians.
walkthrough:
Identify the point in the shaded region giving the least argument $\arg z$:
$$\text{In the fourth quadrant, the least argument (most clockwise from the positive real axis)}$$
$$\text{occurs at the lowest point of the region, where the line } x = 2 \text{ intersects the bottom of the circle.}$$

Find the Cartesian coordinates of this point by substituting $x = 2$ into the circle equation $(x - 1)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 2^2$:
$$(2 - 1)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 4$$
$$1 + (y + 2)^2 = 4 \implies (y + 2)^2 = 3$$
$$y + 2 = \pm\sqrt{3} \implies y = -2 \pm \sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{The lowest point has } y = -2 - \sqrt{3} \approx -2 - 1.73205 = -3.73205$$

Calculate the argument of the complex number $z = 2 - (2 + \sqrt{3})\mathrm{i}$:
$$\arg z = -\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3.73205}{2}\right) = -\tan^{-1}(1.866025)$$
$$\arg z \approx -61.82^{\circ} \approx -61.8^{\circ} \quad (\text{or } -1.08 \text{ radians, or } 298.2^{\circ})$$

State the least value of $\arg z$:
$$-61.8^{\circ} \quad (\text{or } -1.08 \text{ radians})$$
